extracted.intended_audience: meme creators, social-media posters/curators, internet-humor writers, and readers interested in how memes/jokes spread
extracted.subtask_description: A practical rubric for evaluating or creating internet jokes/memes (what makes them funny, spreadable, or poisonous), aimed at memers, social-account operators, and analysts of online humor.

rubrics_metrics.name: Surface joke
rubrics_metrics.description: What a normal person sees.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The immediate, literal punchline or image — should land for someone unfamiliar with the template. (Echoed in the working rubric: 'Does it work on the surface for someone who's never seen the format?')

rubrics_metrics.name: Format joke
rubrics_metrics.description: Recognizing the meme template, getting the meta-laugh.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The joke depends on recognition of a template or format; rewards viewers who know the template. (Related working rubric item: 'Does it reward recognition of the format?')

rubrics_metrics.name: Posting-context joke
rubrics_metrics.description: The joke is partly that someone posted it HERE, NOW.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Context of platform, audience, or timing contributes to the laugh — where and when it's posted is part of the joke. (Related: 'Does it signal where you post from?' and 'Is the timing tied to a current event or moment?')

rubrics_metrics.name: Layer combination (surface/format/context)
rubrics_metrics.description: The funniest posts hit all three layers; mass-shared posts hit at least two.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Scoring note: presence of multiple layers increases comedic payoff and shareability; lacking layers reduces impact.

rubrics_metrics.name: Recognizable template (low cognitive cost)
rubrics_metrics.description: Recognizable template → low cognitive cost to receive.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Memes that use familiar templates are easier to understand and thus spread more readily. Low cognitive load encourages quick consumption and sharing.

rubrics_metrics.name: Adaptability
rubrics_metrics.description: Adaptable → users can substitute their own subject.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Templates that allow easy substitution (text/image swaps, variable punchlines) enable wide remixing and personalization, which fuels spread.

rubrics_metrics.name: In-group signaling
rubrics_metrics.description: In-group flag → posting it signals which corner of the internet you live in.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Memes function as identity markers; successful jokes can signal membership in subcultures or communities and thereby propagate within those groups.

rubrics_metrics.name: Time-boundness
rubrics_metrics.description: Time-bound → the laugh decays after the moment passes.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Topicality increases immediate impact but shortens lifespan. Timing tied to current events or moments makes jokes land harder but also become obsolete faster. (Related working rubric item: 'Is the timing tied to a current event or moment?')

rubrics_metrics.name: Format recency mismatch (too new)
rubrics_metrics.description: The format is too new for half the recipients.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Anti-pattern: using a brand-new or hyper-niche template can fail because many recipients lack the recognition needed to appreciate the joke.

rubrics_metrics.name: Format staleness (too old / cringe)
rubrics_metrics.description: The format is too old (cringe to post unironically).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Anti-pattern: using an overused or outdated template can render a post cringe or unshareable; freshness matters.

rubrics_metrics.name: Misuse of template
rubrics_metrics.description: The poster mis-uses the template's structure.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Anti-pattern: incorrect application of a meme's internal rules (timing, caption structure, image pairing) breaks the joke and signals unfamiliarity with the format.

rubrics_metrics.name: Explaining the joke
rubrics_metrics.description: The post explains itself.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Anti-pattern: explicit explanation kills the comedic effect and signals weakness; the working rubric reiterates 'Did you NOT explain the joke?' as a core criterion.

rubrics_metrics.name: Curation / remix craft (screenshot as unit)
rubrics_metrics.description: The internet's dominant comedy unit is the screenshot of someone else's joke; the remixer is the comedian.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Quality depends on curation choices: which juxtaposition, which crop, and which context are chosen. The crop or screenshot itself can add a layer of meaning (working rubric item: 'Does the crop or screenshot itself add a layer?').

rubrics_metrics.name: Restraint (knowing when not to post)
rubrics_metrics.description: The shitposter's most underrated skill is restraint — knowing when NOT to post.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Good posters exercise judgment about timing, audience tolerance, and potential backlash; refraining can be as important as posting.

rubrics_metrics.name: Ratio as objective metric
rubrics_metrics.description: The ratio is the only objective metric.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Quantitative signal of reception (e.g., upvotes vs. replies/criticisms) is presented as the clearest hard metric for how a post performed; useful for post-hoc evaluation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Brand accounts and edge sustainability
rubrics_metrics.description: Personas (the Wendy's account era) collapsed because corporations can't sustain edge.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Guidance for brands: corporate accounts struggle to maintain authentic 'edge' over time; this affects viability of persona-driven humor and suggests limits for brand-led shitposting.

rubrics_metrics.name: Garbage Day Working Rubric — 1. Surface reception
rubrics_metrics.description: Does it work on the surface for someone who's never seen the format?
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Verbatim working-rubric criterion: prioritize literal comprehensibility for newcomers as a baseline for humor.

rubrics_metrics.name: Garbage Day Working Rubric — 2. Format recognition reward
rubrics_metrics.description: Does it reward recognition of the format?
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Verbatim working-rubric criterion: the joke should give extra payoff to those who recognize the meme/template.

rubrics_metrics.name: Garbage Day Working Rubric — 3. Identity signaling
rubrics_metrics.description: Does it signal where you post from?
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Verbatim working-rubric criterion: the post should communicate in-group/identity context appropriate to the poster/audience.

rubrics_metrics.name: Garbage Day Working Rubric — 4. Timing
rubrics_metrics.description: Is the timing tied to a current event or moment?
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Verbatim working-rubric criterion: topicality is a key factor in impact and shareability.

rubrics_metrics.name: Garbage Day Working Rubric — 5. No explanation
rubrics_metrics.description: Did you NOT explain the joke?
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Verbatim working-rubric criterion: avoid metacomments or explicit explanations that undercut the humor.

rubrics_metrics.name: Garbage Day Working Rubric — 6. Crop/screenshot adds layer
rubrics_metrics.description: Does the crop or screenshot itself add a layer?
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Verbatim working-rubric criterion: consider how framing, cropping, and the screenshot-as-object can contribute an additional comedic dimension.
